card.name: Dose-adjustment verbs after CYP inducer statements
card.fires_on: The verb or linking word that begins a dose-change instruction, such as "consider", "increasing", or "to", right after a mention of a CYP3A4 inducer or inhibitor being stopped or used. It appears in drug-interaction dosing sections.

modes.label: After inducer stopped
modes.description: The word "consider" follows a clause saying a CYP3A4 inducer or inhibitor is discontinued.
modes.example: If a CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued,<< consider>> Hydrocodone Bitartrate and

modes.label: The instruction to increase the dose
modes.description: "increasing" follows "Consider" in advice about strong CYP inducers.
modes.example: Consider<< increasing>> the dose of TRINTELLIX

modes.label: The phrase "may be required to"
modes.description: The word "to" or "be" follows a phrase saying a dose change may be needed or considered.
modes.example: dosage modification may be required<< to>> manage interactions with some concomitant medications

card.plain: It responds to the spot where a label starts to say the dose may need to be changed because of interacting drugs.
evidence: If a CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued,<< consider>> buprenorphine and nalox
Consider<< increasing>> the dose of TRINTELLIX
